findings.source_quote: τοῖς τῇ λύσει θανόντων σωμάτων σκύλλουσιν τὰς ψυχάς
findings.english_quote: those who harass souls by releasing them from dead bodies
findings.issue: The English explicitly makes the harassers agents of releasing souls from bodies. An instrumental interpretation of τῇ λύσει does not by itself establish that agency or the supplied object “them”: λύσις is qualified by θανόντων σωμάτων. The note discloses a bodily-dissolution alternative, but its grammatical rationale does not adequately support the main text’s more specific causal claim.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “those who harass souls at the dissolution of dead bodies.” Preserve the instrumental alternative “through the dissolution of dead bodies” and explain any proposed release-from-bodies interpretation separately, without automatically making the necromancers agents of that release. This is an interpretive issue, not evidence of source corruption.

findings.source_quote: ὡς ἀληθῶς ἀγαθὴ θεοῦ ἄγγελος διέτρεχε τὸν κόσμον
findings.english_quote: like a truly good messenger of God, ran throughout the world
findings.issue: The idiomatic force of ὡς ἀληθῶς is “truly” or “in truth.” The draft instead makes ὡς comparative and scopes “truly” principally over “good,” weakening the report’s personification as genuinely God’s good messenger. The lexical note discusses “messenger” versus “angel” but does not address this change of scope.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “and, truly a good messenger of God, ran throughout the world.” Retain the messenger/angel note. If the comparative construction is retained instead, explicitly compare it with the idiomatic reading and explain the choice.

findings.source_quote: ὃν ποτε εἰσεκλάπην χρόνον ἐλπίσιν δονούμενος
findings.english_quote: the time of which I had been stealthily robbed while being tossed about by hopes
findings.issue: The supplied εἰσεκλάπην is the augmented passive of εἰσκλέπτω, with its inward or surreptitious-entry force. The draft treats χρόνον as the thing stolen rather than considering an accusative of duration: the time during which Clement had been stealthily drawn in or inveigled. Context supports wasted time, but does not alone establish the draft’s particular construction. The note’s purportedly more literal alternative repeats “robbed” and does not disclose this material duration reading.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “the time during which I had been stealthily drawn in, tossed about by hopes.” Explain the duration construction and preserve the loss-of-time interpretation only with an explicit lexical and syntactic basis. Retain εἰσεκλάπην as supplied; unfamiliar usage here is not grounds for another print check or an invented correction.

findings.source_quote: περὶ δὲ τοῦ ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ γενομένου καὶ υἱοῦ θεοῦ ὑπὸ τῆς φήμης λεγομένου καὶ παρὰ πολλῶν τῶν κἀκεῖθεν ἐληλυθότων ἠκούσαμεν
findings.english_quote: But we have heard about the one who appeared in Judea and whom the report calls the Son of God, both from the report itself and from many who have come from there
findings.issue: ὑπὸ τῆς φήμης explicitly identifies the source of the designation “Son of God”; it is not a separately expressed source of ἠκούσαμεν. The draft fills the unexpressed comparison behind additive καὶ παρὰ πολλῶν with “both from the report itself.” That inference is not compelled: the comparison could also include Clement’s just-related account. No note discloses this expansion.
findings.suggested_revision: Proposed for fresh review: “But about the one who was in Judea and whom the report calls the Son of God, we have heard also from many who have come from there as well.” Preserve the additive wording without specifying an unexpressed first source. Any retained report-source interpretation needs its inference and viable alternatives disclosed.
